verses.sanskrit:
कर्ण उवाच।
              भगवन्तमहं भक्तो यथा मां वेत्थ गोपते। तथा परमतिग्मांशो नास्त्यदेयं कथञ्चन॥१॥
verses.english: Karna said: O god, O lord of splendour and scorching rays, you are as much aware of my being a worshipper of yours, (as of the fact) that there is nothing which I can not part with.

verses.sanskrit:
सूर्य उवाच।
              यदि तात ददास्येते वज्रिणे कुण्डले शुभे। त्वमप्येनमथो ब्रूया विजयार्थं महाबलम्॥१॥
verses.english: Karna said: O god, O lord of splendour and scorching rays, you are as much aware of my being a worshipper of yours, (as of the fact) that there is nothing which I can not part with.

verses.sanskrit: न मे दारा न मे पुत्रा न चात्मा सुहृदो न च। तथेष्ठा वै सदा भक्त्या यथा त्वं गोपते मम॥२॥
verses.english: By virtue of the reverence that I always feel for you, you are. O lord of splendour, dearer (to me) then my wife, my sons, my own self and my friends.

verses.sanskrit: इष्टानां च महात्मानो भक्तानां च न संशयः। कुर्वन्ति भक्तिमिष्टां च जानीषे त्वं च भास्कर॥३॥
verses.english: O author of light, you are no doubt aware that high-souled persons cherish a high regard for their devoted worshipper.

verses.sanskrit: इष्टो भक्तश्च मे कर्णो न चान्यद्दैवतं दिवि। जानीत इति वै कृत्वा भगवानाह मद्धितम्॥४॥
verses.english: Considering that Karna is your devoted worshipper and that he known no other god in heavens, you have given me these instructions.

verses.sanskrit: भूयश्च शिरसा याचे प्रसाद्य च पुनः पुनः। इति ब्रवीमि तिग्मांशो त्वं तु मे क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥५॥
verses.english: Again with bended head and repeated prayers do I implore you and tell you this. O lord of searching rays, that you will (graciously) pardon me.

verses.sanskrit: बिभेमि न तथा मृत्योर्यथा बिभ्येऽनृतादहम्। विशेषेण द्विजातीनां सर्वेषां सर्वदा सताम्॥६॥
verses.english: I do not fear death so much as falsehood. Especially for the sake of all the righteous twice-born ones ever, I am ready to sacrifice my life without (the least) hesitation.

verses.sanskrit: प्रदाने जीवितस्यापि न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा। यच्च मामात्थ देव त्वं पाण्डवं फाल्गुनं प्रति॥७॥
verses.english: As to what you have said to me about the Pandava Falguna. O author light, (I ask you) to dispel your caused by mental uneasiness regarding Arjuna and myself. (Because) I will surely defeat Arjuna in battle.

verses.sanskrit: व्येतु सन्तापजं दुःखं तव भास्कर मानसम्। अर्जुनं प्रति मां चैव विजेष्यामि रणेऽर्जुनम्॥८॥
तवापि विदितं देव ममाप्यस्त्रबलं महत्। जामदग्न्यादुपात्तं यत् तथा द्रोणान्महात्मनः॥९॥
verses.english: O god, you are no doubt aware of the great strength of my weapons which I have obtained from the son of Jamadagni (i.e. Parashuram) and from the high-souled Drona.

verses.sanskrit: इदं त्वमनुजानीहि सुरश्रेष्ठ व्रतं मम। भिक्षते वाज्रिणे दद्यामपि जीवितमात्मनः॥१०॥
verses.english: O best of the gods, permit me now to observe the vow on my part that I may bestow my very life upon the begging wielder of the thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit: नियमेन प्रदद्यां ते कुण्डले वै शतक्रतो। अवध्यो ह्यसि भूतानां कुण्डलाभ्यां समन्वितः॥१२॥
verses.english: Surya said: O highly-powerful son, if you bestow your beautiful car-rings to the wielder of the sorrow thunderbolt, you should, in order to secure victory, say to him, “O lord of hundred sacrifices, I can only part with my ear-rings under a condition."

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनेन विनाशं हि तव दानवसूदनः। प्रार्थयानो रणे वत्स कुण्डले ते जिहीर्षति॥१३॥
verses.english: As you cannot surely be slain by any creature when furnished with your earrings, so the destroyer of the Danavas, O son, wishing your death at the hands of Arjuna in battle, wants to rob you of your ear-rings.

verses.sanskrit: स त्वमप्येनमाराध्य सूनृताभिः पुनः पुनः। अभ्यर्थयेथा देवेशममोघार्थं पुरन्दरम्॥१४॥
verses.english: Worshipping again and again with agreeable and truthful speeches the lord of the celestials, Purandara, the possessor of infallible weapons.

verses.sanskrit: अमोघां देहि मे शक्तिममित्रविनिबर्हिणीम्। दास्यामि ते सहस्राक्ष कुण्डले वर्म चोत्तमम्॥१५॥
verses.english: You will say to him, “O thousand-eyed lord, I will give you the two ear-rings and the excellent armour, if you will bestow on me an infallible dart destructive of enemies."

verses.sanskrit: इत्येव नियमेन त्वं दद्याः शक्राय कुण्डले। तया त्वं कर्ण सङ्ग्रामे हनिष्यास रणे रिपून्॥१६॥
verses.english: It is under this condition only, O Karna, that you will give your ear-rings to Shakra. Then you will be able to destroy your enemies in battle.

verses.sanskrit: नाहत्वा हि महाबाहो शत्रूनेति करं पुनः। सा शक्तिर्देवराजस्य शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥१७॥
verses.english: O mighty-armed one, that arrow of the lord of the gods does not return to the hand of the person who discharges it, without destroying hundreds and thousands of enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्त्वा सहस्त्रांशुः सहसाऽन्तरधीयत। ततः सूर्याय जप्यान्ते कर्णः स्वप्नं न्यवेदयत्॥१८॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Saying this, the lord of thousand rays suddenly became invisible. (The next day) Karna after having performed his devotions told the sun of the dreara.

verses.sanskrit: यथा दृष्टं यथातत्वं यथोक्तमुभयोर्निशि। तत्सर्वमानुपूर्व्येण शशंसास्मै वृषस्तदा॥१९॥
verses.english: And Vrisha (Karna) faithfully related to him everything in detail, viz. his meeting with the sun and the conversation that took place between them during the nighi.

verses.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान् देवो भानुः स्वर्भानुसूदनः। उवाच तं तथेत्येव कर्णं सूर्यः स्मयन्निव॥२०॥
verses.english: Hearing all this, the divine lord Bhanu, the subduer of Svarbhanu (Rahu) spoke to Karna with a smile, "it is all true.”

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तत्त्वमिति ज्ञात्वा राधेयः परवीरहा। शक्तिमेवाभिकाङ्क्षन् वै वासवं प्रत्यपालयत्॥२१॥
verses.english: Then the son of Radha, the slayer of enemies, knowing all this to be true, awaited (the arrival of) Vasava, with the desire of obtaining the dart.
